title: Cap. IV Arg. 4: Eph. 1:4 — election in Christ is of believers only; Arminius Exam. Pred. Perk.
latin: Arg. 4. Aliud argumentum petitur ex Eph. i. 4. Sicut nos elegit in ipso, scil. Christo. Unde sic argumentantur; Electio qua nos elegit in Christo Deus, est tantum credentium: Electio quae facta est ante jacta mundi fundamenta facta est in Christo: Ergo illa credentium tantum est. Majoris veritas ex eo apparet, quod nemo in Christo eligi potest, nisi qui in Christo est, quales sunt soli credentes. Hoc idem argumentum urgitur ab Arminio in Exam. Pred. Perk. pag. 313, 32. ubi haec verba habet, Christus secundum Apostolum, non tantum est medium per quod salus electione jam ante parta obtinetur, sed tanquam causa meritoria, cujus respectu electio facta sit, et propter quem illa gratia sit praeparata. Deus enim neminem ad vitam aeternam amat nisi in Christo: Ex quo sequi videtur, quod cum nemo in Christo consideretur a Deo, nisi ille sit insertus per fidem, Fidelium propria sit electio. Haec ille.
pass_a: Argument 4. Another argument is sought from Eph. 1:4. According as he chose us in him, namely Christ. Whence they argue thus; The election by which God chose us in Christ is only of believers: The election which was made before the foundations of the world were laid was made in Christ: Therefore that is only of believers. The truth of the Major appears from this, that no one can be elected in Christ, except one who is in Christ, of which sort are believers alone. This same argument is urged by Arminius in Exam. Pred. Perk. pages 313, 32, where he has these words, Christ according to the Apostle is not only a means through which salvation already beforehand obtained by election is gotten, but as a meritorious cause, in respect of which election may have been made, and for whom that grace may have been prepared. For God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ: From which it seems to follow, that since no one is considered in Christ by God, unless he be inserted through faith, election is proper to the faithful. These things he.
pass_b: Arg. 4. Another argument from Eph. 1:4 — According as he chose us in him, that is Christ. They argue: the election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only; the election made before the world's foundations was made in Christ; therefore it is of believers only. The Major's truth, they say, is that no one can be elected in Christ unless he is in Christ — and only believers are. Arminius urges the same in Exam. Pred. Perk. pp. 313, 32: on the Apostle, Christ is not only a means through which salvation already gotten by election is obtained, but a meritorious cause in respect of which election is made and for whom that grace is prepared. God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ; so since no one is considered in Christ by God unless inserted by faith, election belongs to the faithful. So he.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: conclusion misses the point — believers consequently, not antecedently; Augustine
latin: Sol. Ab ipsa conclusione ordiamur responsionem nostram. Dicimus ergo, non concludi illud quod positum est in controversia. Non enim quaeritur utrum electio sit solummodo eorum qui credentes sunt futuri, vel, quod eodem recidit, eorum quos Deus ante jacta mundi fundamenta praevidet credituros; sed utrum aeternus ille actus electionis Divinae praerequirat hanc praevisionem tanquam causam, aut saltem conditionem antecedaneam: quod nos negamus, et adversarii neutiquam possunt probare. Concedimus illis, Electionem esse tantum credentium; sed non credentium in praescientia Divina antecedenter ad ipsam electionem, sed credentium in praescientia Divina consequenter, et virtute gratiae in electione illis praeparatae et destinatae, juxta illud Augustini De Praed. Sanct. cap. 18, Ideo tales eramus futuri quia elegit ipse ut tales per gratiam essemus. Et cap. 10. Praedestinatione Deus praescivit quid fuerat ipse facturus. Consimilia habet cap. 17. Quae loca Augustini si quis consulat, et Arminiani hujus argumenti optimam solutionem, et Paulini hujus contextus optimam explicationem inveniet.
pass_a: Solution. Let us begin our response from the conclusion itself. We say therefore that that is not concluded which is posited in the controversy. For it is not asked whether election is only of those who will be believers, or, which comes to the same, of those whom God before the foundations of the world were laid foresees will believe; but whether that eternal act of the Divine election prerequires this foresight as a cause, or at least an antecedent condition: which we deny, and the adversaries can by no means prove. We concede to them that Election is only of believers; but not of believers in the Divine foresight antecedently to the election itself, but of believers in the Divine foresight consequently, and by virtue of the grace prepared and destined for them in the election, according to that of Augustine On the Predestination of the Saints chapter 18, Therefore we were going to be such because he himself chose that we should be such through grace. And chapter 10. By predestination God foresaw what he himself was going to do. He has like things in chapter 17. Which places of Augustine if anyone consults, he will find both the best solution of this Arminian argument, and the best explanation of this Pauline context.
pass_b: Sol. Start from their conclusion: it does not settle what is in controversy. The question is not whether election is only of those who will be believers — or of those God foresaw before the world's foundations would believe — but whether that eternal act of divine election prerequires that foresight as cause, or at least antecedent condition. We deny it; adversaries cannot prove it. We grant election is of believers only — not believers in divine foresight before election, but believers consequently, by virtue of the grace prepared and destined for them in election. So Augustine, De praed. Sanct. 18: we were going to be such because he chose that we should be such through grace; and ch. 10: by predestination God foresaw what he himself would do (likewise ch. 17). Consult those places for the best solution of this Arminian argument and the best reading of this Pauline context.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: Major — temporal election of actual believers vs eternal gift of faith in Christ
latin: Sed missa conclusionis ventilatione accedo ad Majorem; quae fuit hujusmodi, Electio qua nos Deus elegit in Christo est tantum credentium. Si de electione temporali, qua certae personae per vocationem efficacem a mundo improborum secernuntur, intelligatur haec propositio, agnoscimus hanc electionem esse tantum credentium, et actualiter credentium: sed nos de aeterno electionis Divinae actu, non de temporali ejusdem effectu, disputamus. Si ergo hanc aeternam electionem respiciant, quam in hac controversia respicere debent, dicimus hanc electionem non esse credentium, quasi quidam homines extra Christum adhuc constituti praeviderentur a Deo ut credentes, et interveniente hac fide praevisa eligerentur; sed esse credentium, quia Deus praevidit se illis donum fidei daturum, quos in aeterno electionis proposito Christo dare decrevit.
pass_a: But the ventilation of the conclusion having been dismissed I come to the Major; which was of this sort, The election by which God chose us in Christ is only of believers. If this proposition be understood of temporal election, by which certain persons are severed from the world of the wicked through efficacious vocation, we acknowledge that this election is only of believers, and of actually believing ones: but we dispute concerning the eternal act of the Divine election, not concerning the temporal effect of the same. If therefore they regard this eternal election, which in this controversy they ought to regard, we say that this election is not of believers, as if certain men still constituted outside Christ were foreseen by God as believers, and with this foreseen faith intervening were elected; but is of believers, because God foresaw that he would give the gift of faith to those whom in the eternal purpose of election he decreed to give to Christ.
pass_b: Drop the conclusion and take the Major: The election by which God chose us in Christ is of believers only. If that means temporal election — certain persons severed from the wicked world by efficacious vocation — we grant it is of believers, and of actually believing ones. But we dispute the eternal act of divine election, not its temporal effect. So of eternal election (what this controversy must regard): it is not of believers as if men still outside Christ were foreseen as believers and then elected with that foresight intervening; it is of believers because God foresaw he would give the gift of faith to those he decreed in the eternal purpose of election to give to Christ.

lemmas.gloss: gift of faith in eternal purpose

title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: John 6:37 — donation causes coming; elegit in Christo mis-exposed
latin: Huc faciunt illa Christi verba apud Johannem vi. 37. Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet. Donatio haec aeternam Dei electionem designat: Venire, fidem in humanis cordibus suo tempore productam denotat: a donatio innuitur causa antecedanea veniendi, id est, credendi: non autem fides praevisa causa antecedanea donandi, hoc est, eligendi. Quod autem afferunt ad Majoris confirmationem, Deum non posse illum eligere in Christo qui non est in Christo: Illi autem tantum in Christo sunt, qui a Deo considerantur ut Christo inserti per fidem: ergo soli credentes eliguntur: haec argumentatio nititur falsa expositione illorum verborum Apostolicorum, Elegit nos in Christo.
pass_a: Hither avail those words of Christ at John 6:37. Whatever the Father gives me will come to me. This donation designates the eternal election of God: To come denotes faith produced in human hearts in its time: from the donation is hinted the antecedent cause of coming, that is, of believing: but not foreseen faith the antecedent cause of giving, that is, of electing. But what they bring for confirmation of the Major, That God cannot elect in Christ him who is not in Christ: But those only are in Christ who are considered by God as inserted into Christ through faith: therefore believers alone are elected: this argumentation rests on a false exposition of those Apostolic words, He chose us in Christ.
pass_b: John 6:37 helps here: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me. The donation marks God's eternal election; coming marks faith produced in human hearts in its time. Donation is the antecedent cause of coming (believing) — not foreseen faith the antecedent cause of giving (electing). Their Major confirmation — God cannot elect in Christ one who is not in Christ; only those considered inserted into Christ by faith are in Christ; therefore only believers are elected — rests on a false reading of He chose us in Christ.

title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol: in Christo refers to the electing act — Eph. 1:3, 2 Cor. 5:19 parallels
latin: Nam illa verba, in Christo, non ad statum hominis electi, sed ad actum eligentis Dei sunt referenda. Arminiani sic exponunt, Elegit nos in Christo, id est, Nos existentes in Christo, vel nos consideratos et praevisos ut credentes in Christum, et per fidem in illum insertos, Deus postmodum elegit. Sed haec loquendi formula, in Christo, quoties conjungitur cum aliquo actu Divino, non semper innuit subjectum, in quod tendit ille actus, considerari ut existens in Christo antecedenter. Verbi causa, Eph. i. 3. Deus benedixit nobis omni benedictione spirituali in Christo. At inter spirituales benedictiones est ipsa prima fidei et poenitentiae donatio, quae non dantur existentibus in Christo, sed alienis a Christo, ut ad Christum adducantur, et ei inserantur. Sic Deus dicitur in Christo mundum sibi reconciliasse, 2 Cor. v. 19; in Christo ad bona opera nos condidisse, Eph. ii. 10. Denique ipsi Remonstrantes docent Deum regenerare homines in Christo, Coll. pag. 99. In hisce omnibus locis verba illa, in Christo, non possunt nisi absurdissime exponi, in Christo antecedenter existentes. Eligere igitur in Christo nil aliud est, quam in eligendo respicere ad Christum Mediatorem et Caput Ecclesiae, ejusque gratia membra illi conjungenda et glorificanda destinare.
pass_a: For those words, in Christ, are to be referred not to the state of the elect man, but to the act of the electing God. The Arminians so expose, He chose us in Christ, that is, Us existing in Christ, or us considered and foreseen as believing in Christ, and inserted into him through faith, God afterward chose. But this form of speaking, in Christ, as often as it is joined with some Divine act, does not always hint that the subject toward which that act tends is considered as existing in Christ antecedently. For example, Eph. 1:3. God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ. But among spiritual blessings is the very first donation of faith and repentance, which are not given to those existing in Christ, but to those alien from Christ, that they may be led to Christ, and inserted into him. So God is said in Christ to have reconciled the world to himself, 2 Cor. 5:19; in Christ to have created us unto good works, Eph. 2:10. Finally the Remonstrants themselves teach that God regenerates men in Christ, Coll. p. 99. In all these places those words, in Christ, cannot except most absurdly be exposed as existing in Christ antecedently. To elect therefore in Christ is nothing else than in electing to look to Christ the Mediator and Head of the Church, and by his grace to destine members to be joined to him and glorified.
pass_b: In Christ refers not to the elect man's state but to the electing God's act. Arminians expose He chose us in Christ as: us already existing in Christ, or foreseen as believing and inserted by faith, whom God then chose. But in Christ joined to a divine act does not always mean the subject already exists in Christ beforehand. Eph. 1:3: God blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ — and among those blessings is the first gift of faith and repentance, given not to those already in Christ but to those alien from him, to bring them to Christ and insert them. So God in Christ reconciled the world to himself (2 Cor. 5:19) and created us unto good works (Eph. 2:10). Remonstrants themselves say God regenerates men in Christ (Coll. p. 99). In all these, in Christ cannot without absurdity mean already existing in Christ beforehand. So to elect in Christ is nothing but, in electing, to look to Christ the Mediator and Head of the Church, and by his grace to destine members to be joined to him and glorified.

lemmas.gloss: in Christ of the electing act
Mediator and Head of the Church

title: Cap. IV Arg. 4 Sol close: love to eternal life in Christ true of introduction, false of praedestinatio
latin: Quod autem Arminius urget, Deum neminem amare ad vitam aeternam nisi in Christo, hoc est, ut ille interpretatur, nisi consideratum ut fidelem, et jam Christo insertum, ac proinde neminem eligere nisi qua fidelem; id de ipsa introductione ad vitam aeternam verum est, sed de praedestinatione falsum. Nam Deus illos omnes hoc sensu ad vitam aeternam amat, quos Christo vivificandos et servandos ante jacta mundi fundamenta dare decrevit. Hi autem qui dantur vivificandi, non considerantur a Deo ut vivificati et fideles, sed ut in peccatis mortui et adhuc infideles. Ut absolvam verbo; Deus dicitur nos elegisse in Christo, non quia consideravit nos tanquam per fidem nostram in Christo existentes, antequam eligeremur, sed quia cum respectu ad Christum Mediatorem ad vitam aeternam praedestinantur quotquot praedestinantur.
pass_a: But what Arminius urges, That God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ, that is, as he interprets, except considered as faithful, and already inserted into Christ, and therefore elects no one except as faithful; that is true of the introduction itself to eternal life, but false of predestination. For God in this sense loves to eternal life all those whom before the foundations of the world were laid he decreed to give to Christ to be made alive and saved. But these who are given to be made alive are not considered by God as made alive and faithful, but as dead in sins and still unbelieving. To finish in a word; God is said to have chosen us in Christ, not because he considered us as existing in Christ through our faith, before we were elected, but because with respect to Christ the Mediator whoever are predestinated are predestinated to eternal life.
pass_b: Arminius urges that God loves no one to eternal life except in Christ — as he reads it, except considered faithful and already inserted into Christ, and so elects none except as faithful. That is true of the introduction itself to eternal life, false of predestination. In that sense God loves to eternal life all he decreed before the world's foundations to give to Christ to be made alive and saved. Those given to be made alive are not considered already made alive and faithful, but dead in sins and still unbelieving. In a word: God chose us in Christ not because he viewed us as already in Christ by our faith before election, but because with respect to Christ the Mediator all who are predestinated are predestinated to eternal life.

lemmas.gloss: true of introduction, false of predestination
